title: Quinze Respostas: Every Kairos League Player's Pick, One Secret, and a Ban Forever
subtitle: A Riot Games pre-season roster feature with all fifteen Kairos League players, Main, Blue, and White alike.
summary: Fifteen Kairos League players sit for a Riot Games pre-season feature: one signature champion, one personal fact each, and a closing group round naming the champion they would ban forever.

content.text: This article is a fictional dramatization written for the Kairos Universe story. It is formatted in the style of a Riot Games roster feature, but it is not an actual Riot Games publication, product, or statement.

Before the 2027 season, a small Riot Games crew spent an afternoon at the [[organization:kairos-esports|Kairos]] campus with all fifteen League players across [[team:kairos-lol-main|Kairos Main]], [[team:kairos-lol-academy-blue|Kairos Academy Blue]], and [[team:kairos-lol-academy-white|Kairos Academy White]]. Each player answered two questions: which champion they would choose to represent themselves, and one thing a fan who follows them probably doesn't know yet. At the end, all fifteen were asked, on camera and without preparation, which champion they would ban forever.
Kairos Main

[[player:noah-rkn-bennett|Noah "rkN" Bennett]] named Fiora without hesitation: "If I lose, I usually know what I did wrong. If I win, I also know what I did right. I like that." His personal fact turned out to be a habit, not a confession: he watches his own lane replays with the sound off, so he can check whether a decision still reads as logical without anyone explaining it afterward.

[[player:ethan-vanta-walker|Ethan "Vanta" Walker]] picked Lee Sin, with Nidalee and Kindred close behind, because he likes champions that let him change the shape of a fight before it starts. Off camera, teammates learned he has a standing habit of mentally reconstructing the enemy jungler's path after a game before he ever opens the replay, just to see afterward if he had it right.

[[player:mason-404-brooks|Mason "404" Brooks]] surprised the crew with Orianna over anything flashier: "You can control a fight without being near it." Syndra and Azir are close seconds. His trivia answer was a collection of seven old mechanical keyboards — not a large number, he insisted, but old enough that some of them predate a few of his White teammates.

[[player:liam-aster-oconnor|Liam "Aster" O'Connor]] answered Kai'Sa immediately: "You can play aggressive without having to play dumb." Xayah is another favorite. His personal fact ran against type for an ADC: he dislikes watching his own pentakills back, because there's always something ugly buried in the middle of them.

[[player:daniel-moss-reyes|Daniel "Moss" Reyes]] closed out Main with Thresh — "basically everything he does depends on someone else doing something afterward" — with Braum and Rakan not far behind. Asked for something fans wouldn't know, he produced a small black notebook he's kept since before Kairos: not full strategies, just names, habits, and timings he's observed on opposing supports.
Kairos Academy Blue

[[player:connor-mako-sullivan|Connor "SullCon" Sullivan]] chose Renekton — he likes a lane that starts early — with Camille behind it. His trivia answer was about his own nickname: a straightforward contraction of Sullivan and Connor, settled, by his own account, in about thirty seconds.

[[player:jacob-xnox-price|Jacob "xNox" Price]] named Nidalee — "if I'm playing well, it feels like I'm everywhere" — with Lee Sin close behind. He revealed he built his first computer mostly from used parts at thirteen years old, and declined to say much more about the first motherboard.

[[player:owen-kite-hughes|Owen "Kite" Hughes]] picked Azir — "I like controlling space" — with Viktor and Taliyah close behind. His personal fact landed harder than expected: he has played piano since childhood, something almost nobody at Kairos knew until that afternoon.

[[player:tyler-murmur-grant|Tyler "Murmur" Grant]] answered Ezreal — "you can do idiotic things and sometimes they look like genius" — with Jinx and Aphelios as frequent picks. His trivia fact didn't surprise his teammates at all: he talks to himself constantly in solo queue, because, in his words, he's the only one always in the game.

[[player:lucas-grit-foster|Lucas "japalenogrits" Foster]] closed Blue with Rakan — "get in fast, get out fast, and act like it was planned" — with Bard another favorite. His trivia answer finally confirmed the story behind his nickname for the public: a particularly bad personal experience involving jalapeños and grits.
Kairos Academy White

[[player:isaac-pebble-young|Isaac "Pebble" Young]] opened White with Ornn — "I can lose lane and still have work to do" — with Sion close behind. His trivia fact was a small, carried habit: a smooth stone he keeps in his backpack from before he ever joined Kairos, which he admitted might just be superstition after all.

[[player:benjamin-vex-carter|Benjamin "vexemite" Carter]] named Kindred — "I like having to decide how far something is worth going for" — with Vi a frequent comfort pick. His trivia answer traced his own nickname: he tried Vegemite exactly once, rated it a minus-two out of ten, and saw no reason to try it again.

[[player:nathan-0bit-hall|Nathan "0bit" Hall]] picked Viktor — "I like a champion that improves alongside the game" — with Orianna second. His trivia fact fit his nickname well: a collection of old handheld consoles, including a Game Boy, a DS, and a PSP, some working better than others.

[[player:cole-june-mercer|Cole "June" Mercer]] answered Jhin — "four shots, that's enough" — with Caitlyn a likely second. His personal fact explained his own nickname: born on June 2nd, he used his birth month as a handle when he first started playing online, and never changed it.

[[player:ryan-luma-chen|Ryan "Luma" Chen]] closed the fifteen with Bard — Milio and Lulu are other favorites — and the quietest trivia answer of the day: he likes photographing city lights at night, mostly, and has hundreds of photos on his phone that he almost never posts, because he took them to see, not to be seen.
One champion, banned forever
Riot's crew closed the session by bringing all fifteen players back together for one unscripted question, asked on camera with no time to prepare: which champion would you ban forever?

items: rkN (Noah Bennett): Malphite
Vanta (Ethan Walker): Shaco
404 (Mason Brooks): Fizz
Aster (Liam O'Connor): Draven
Moss (Daniel Reyes): Yuumi
SullCon (Connor Sullivan): Vayne, specifically top lane
xNox (Jacob Price): Shaco
Kite (Owen Hughes): LeBlanc
Murmur (Tyler Grant): Yasuo
japalenogrits (Lucas Foster): Pyke
Pebble (Isaac Young): Illaoi
vexemite (Benjamin Carter): Teemo

content.text: Further trivia revealed later

The following facts were not part of this Riot Games filming. They surfaced afterward, in a private conversation among the players themselves once the cameras had left. Kairospedia records them here as separately sourced, author-approved public background — not as additional answers Riot Games asked or filmed, and not as part of this roster feature's original on-camera content.

items: rkN (Noah Bennett): played basketball as a forward in school leagues and still follows the NBA; learned to cook from his mother.
Vanta (Ethan Walker): used to fish with his father for hours; ran cross-country at school.

404 (Mason Brooks): made small, non-public video game mods, including once replacing sound effects with his own phone recordings; attended chess club for about six months before deciding he disliked losing slowly.
Aster (Liam O'Connor): worked part-time in a sporting goods store, handling stock and customer service; played baseball as an outfielder for several years.

Moss (Daniel Reyes): helped his family with food distributions and local community events; is interested in city, metro, road, and railway maps, and likes understanding a city before he travels to it.
SullCon (Connor Sullivan): worked one summer washing cars; watches wrestling, including older eras, but does not practice it.
xNox (Jacob Price): used to dismantle broken electronics, not always able to put them back together; played American football briefly when younger.
Kite (Owen Hughes): started piano around age six at his grandmother's insistence and reads sheet music; likes astronomy and used a small telescope for years in Kelowna.
Murmur (Tyler Grant): grew up skateboarding and claims to still know a few tricks; has edited videos, clips, and montages for friends.
japalenogrits (Lucas Foster): sang in his school choir; helped an uncle at a small diner for months and can cook.
Pebble (Isaac Young): played soccer as a fullback; competed in local school mathematics contests and likes logic problems.
vexemite (Benjamin Carter): was a scout as a child and knows tent setup, knots, and compass navigation; is very skilled at rhythm games.
0bit (Nathan Hall): knows basic soldering and repair for handheld consoles and was in a small school robotics club; teammates recall the collection running to eleven handhelds, including a PSP-3000.
June (Cole Mercer): worked at a movie theater; likes old thriller films and tracks hundreds of them, with scores, in a personal spreadsheet.

Luma (Ryan Chen): started with an old digital camera given to him by his father; photographs rain, buildings, evening lights, and empty campus spaces, and does not automatically publish his personal photos.

notes: The 'Further trivia revealed later' section sources Episode 97, a private post-interview conversation among players, not the Episode 96 Riot filming. Author-approved for public display; must never be presented as Riot-filmed content.
